lyrics:
[Intro: tin whistle melody, frame drum, acoustic guitar]

[Verse 1: clear female voice, bright]
My grandmother counted on her fingers every night
Before she'd lay her head down, before she'd dim the light
One for the bread, and two for the roof
Three for the neighbours, and four for the truth

[Chorus: group voices, fiddle, stomping]
And I'm running out of fingers
I'm running out of hands
Counting up the good you've done
Is more than one girl can
Lend me yours, lend me the stars
Lend me every grain of sand
I'm running out of fingers
And I'm only where I began

[Verse 2: voice softer, whistle answering]
One for a manger, a baby in the hay
Two for a blind man who saw his first day
Three for a table where the traitor got fed
Four for a Friday, and the last thing he said

[Chorus: group voices, fiddle, stomping]
And I'm running out of fingers
I'm running out of hands
Counting up the good you've done
Is more than one girl can
Lend me yours, lend me the stars
Lend me every grain of sand
I'm running out of fingers
And I'm only where I began

[Verse 3: voice lifting, band full]
Five for a Sunday and a stone rolled wide
Six for a breakfast on the waterside
Seven for the day that he calls me home
I'll start again there, with a new set of my own

[Instrumental: whistle and fiddle reel, handclaps]

[Bridge: voices alone, hushed then growing]
Morning, I'll count. Noon, I'll count.
When my voice is gone and I can't get it out
My soul will count

[Final Chorus: everyone, loudest]
Jesus, I'm running out of fingers
I'm running out of hands
Counting up the good you've done
Is more than one girl can
Lend me yours, lend me the stars
Lend me every grain of sand
I'm running out of fingers
And I'm only where I began

[Outro: whistle alone, one voice]
One for the bread...
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 112 BPM, 6/8, D major. A lilting Irish-style jig, light on its feet and easy to clap.

VOICE: Female, clear and unadorned, with a slight lilt, like a folk singer. A group of men, women and children join every chorus in unison and simple harmony. The bridge is voices only.

INSTRUMENTS: Tin whistle, fiddle, a frame drum (bodhran), acoustic guitar in open tuning, mandolin, an accordion drone, upright bass, foot stomps and handclaps.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, whistle tune. 0:12 Verse 1. 0:36 Chorus 1. 1:00 Verse 2, the count changes. 1:24 Chorus 2. 1:48 Verse 3. 2:10 Instrumental reel. 2:26 Bridge, voices alone. 2:42 Final chorus. 3:08 Outro, whistle and the first count again at 3:14.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Folk-pop with a Celtic band: bright, woody, lively, voices recorded together in a room.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'Four for a Friday, and the last thing he said' at 1:20.

THE REVEAL: Verse 1 is a grandmother's nightly habit. Verse 2 at 1:00 keeps the same counting game and fills it with the life of Christ; verse 3 reaches Easter morning and the breakfast on the shore. The name is sung at the start of the last chorus.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Fond, thankful, awed, endless.
